result:
The proposed solution's key claim is wrong: it treats the triangle $C_3$ as satisfying $\mathcal{P}$.

A graph has an induced subdivision of $K_3$ exactly when it has an induced cycle of length at least 3, and every cycle of length at least 3 is such a subdivision. So the graphs with no induced $K_3$-subdivision are exactly the chordal graphs. Chordal graphs have unbounded clique-width (split graphs, a subclass of chordal graphs, already do). Therefore $\mathcal{P}$ fails for $C_3$, so $C_3$ cannot be in $\mathcal{M}$.

The proposed answer depends on $C_3$ being maximal, so its set $\{C_3, P_4\}$ and its sum of 6 cannot be correct. The proposal also gives no justification for its characterization beyond asserting it. I did not verify the full set $\mathcal{M}$ from the literature, so I cannot state the correct sum, but the claimed value 6 rests on a false premise.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 4
